text.p: German utility group IsarAmperwerke (IAW) said on Thursday that, according to preliminary figures, earnings in the year to the end of June 1996 were higher than in the previous year.

The electricity producer did not give details of earnings figures, but said that overall sales fell 1.2 percent to 1.97 billion marks. Operating profits were clearly higher in 1996/97 because of higher revenues and lower write-offs, IAW said.
IAW said its financial result in 96/97 would be lower than in the previous year because of extraordinary factors.

Electricity production grew 0.8 percent to around 10 billion kilowatt hours. Capital investment grew to 250 million marks from 230 million marks, while the number of employees fell by three percent to 2,722 during the year.
Bayernwerk, the Viag unit which is in the process of merging with IAW, now holds 81 percent of votes in IAW, which means IAW has been a unit of Viag since July 1, IAW said.
The group said that in order to match up with Viag, IAW would report a short business year from July 1 1997 to December 31 1997.
